description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives (PDO) are to restore, improve, and enhance resilience of public services, environmental facilities, and livelihoods in Targeted Communities, and to enhance the capacity of state entities to respond promptly and effectively toan eligible crisis or emergency.

The development objectives of the Andhra Pradesh Disaster Recovery Project for India are to restore, improve, and enhance resilience of public services, environmental facilities, and livelihoods in targeted communities, and to enhance the capacity of state entities to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency. The project comprises of seven components. The first component, resilient electrical network objective is to reduce the vulnerability of the city's electrical network by laying the power distribution system underground. The second component, restoration of connectivity and shelter infrastructure will finance investments to permanently restore, upgrade, and increase resilience towards future disasters of roads and cyclone shelters. It consists of following two sub-components: (i) restoration of rural roads and cyclone shelters; and (ii) restoration of major district roads. The third component, restoration and protection of the beach front will support priority investments along the beachfront of the city of Visakhapatnam. It consists of following two sub-components: (i) shore protection works; and (ii) beach front restoration. The fourth component, restoration of environmental services and facilities and livelihood support will finance the reconstruction of the severely damaged Indira Gandhi zoological park (IGZP) at Visakhapatnam and eco-tourism Park at Kambalakonda wildlife sanctuary. It consists of following two sub-components: (i) restoration of environmental services and facilities; and (ii) livelihoods support. The fifth component, capacity building and technical support for disaster risk management will support investments to enhance the capabilities of Government of Andhra Pradesh (GoAP) entities and other stake holders in managing disaster risks, enhancing preparedness, and achieving resilient recovery. It consists of following two sub-components: (i) capacity augmentation for disaster management; and (ii) technical support for risk reduction and response preparedness. The sixth component, project implementation support will finance establishing and operating the project management unit (PMU) and the project implementation units (PIUs). The seventh component, contingency emergency response will draw resources from the unallocated expenditure category and or allow the GoAP to request the Bank to re-categorize and reallocate financing from other project components to partially cover emergency response and recovery costs.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :CER Component | Description :The PIE jointly with India to: (a) determine the occurrence of an eligible crisisor emergency; (b) prepare a component-specific operations manual; (c) identify, strengthen and maintain a coordination authoritycapable of carrying out the activities and responsibilities set forth in the operations manual; and (d) prepare and disclose anyrequired safeguard document. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS
Finance Agreement :Complaints Mechanism | Description :The PIE to establish and/or strengthen, maintain and operate a grievanceredress mechanism at all levels. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Contractors Safeguard Obligations | Description :The PIE to include compliance with the Safeguard Documents aspart of the contractors obligations pursuant to the bidding documents. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Government Permits-Compensation/Relocation Assistance | Description :The PIE to ensure that prior to commencingany civil works: (a) all governmental permits and clearances have been obtained and pre-constructions conditions imposed have beenmet; and (b) all resettlement compensation and relocation assistance has been paid/provided. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Implementation Units-II | Description :The PIE to maintain (a) a SSC for policy guidance and general oversight;and (b) a PMU within the APRDMD for coordinating the day-to-day financial management and reporting under the Project, carrying outthe activities under component 5, monitoring and evaluating the PIUs implementation of other Components, and ensuring compliancewith safeguard documents and the handling of Project grievances. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Implementation Units-III | Description :The PIE to hire a senior finance officer or chartered accountant withskills, qualifications, experience and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Implementing Units -I | Description :PIE to establish, and thereafter maintain, 6 PIUs within EPDCL, PRD, R&BD,GVMC, VUDA, and APFD with adequate resources, to carry out day to day Project activities including cost estimates, procurement andbids related documentation and reports, contracts, government clearances and permits, financial management under their respectiveComponents ensuring enforcement/compliance with safeguard docs. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Ineligible Expenditures | Description :The PIE to pay any land acquisition, and any compensation, resettlementand rehabilitation payments out of its own resources. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Management Information System | Description :PIE to maintain a management information system in form andsubstance satisfactory to the Association, which system shall be updated/expanded in a manner and substance agreed with theAssociation. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Operations Manual | Description :The PIE to prepare and adopt and Operations Manual as agreed with theAssociation, and thereafter, implement the Project in accordance with such manual. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Procurement documentation and record keeping system | Description :The PIE to maintain a fully operationalprocurement documentation and record keeping system, in a manner and substance agreed with the Association, including a freely andpublicly accessible database with an interface (link) with APRDMD's and the Line Departmentsand Agencies websites. | Frequency:CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Resilient Electrical Network | Description :PIE to enter into a written agreement with EPDCL under terms andconditions agreed with the Association to comply with all the fiduciary and safeguard standards, procedures and requirements. |Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Restoration of Environmental Services and Facilities and Livelihood Support | Description :PIE to (i) determineif assistance of one or more Participating Agencies is necessary in the implementation of Component 4; (ii) identify, through APFD,such Participating Agency in a manner agreed with the Association (iii) enter into a written agreement with such ParticipatingAgency under terms and conditions agreed with the Association to comply with all the fiduciary and safeguard standards. | Frequency:CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Safeguard Documents | Description :The PIE to carry out, and cause each of the Line Departments and Agencies tocarry out, the Project in accordance with the ESMF, and the EMP(s), RAP(s), and/or IPDP(s) (the Safeguard Documents). | Frequency:CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Safeguard Reporting & Monitoring | Description :The PIE to: (i) maintain monitoring and evaluation protocols andrecord keeping procedures to supervise and assess compliance with Safeguard Documents; and (ii) report on quarterly basis oncompliance with Safeguard Documents. | Frequency :Quarterly

Finance Agreement :Screening of Activities - Social & Environmental Documents | Description :The PIE to (a) screen (through thePMU/PIUs) any proposed activities as per the ESMF and, whenever required, prepare the necessary EMP(s), RAP(s) and/or IPDP(s); and(b) publicly disclose those safeguards documents, including an executive summary in local language(s) at the relevant project'ssites. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Third Party Quality Consulting Firm(s) | Description :The PIE to select and hire the services of (a) third partyquality consulting firm(s) to carry out quarterly quality monitoring and reporting to the PMU on contract performance andcompliance with and/or implementation of the statutory/regulatory requirements, safeguards documents and Operations Manual. |Frequency :CONTINUOUS

<p>To achieve this result, the project financed the rehabilitation of 186 rural roads including three bridges, of a total length of 563.19 kilometers. <p>Information source: PRD project completion reports and other supplementary documents. </p>

title.narrative: Number of workdays generated to provide improved livelihood support

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved for total number of workdays. (145% achievement compared to the newly added target: 925,585 days compared to 638,000 days)</p>

<p>Target achieved for female. (145% achievement compared to the newly added target: 487,079 days compared to 335,700 days)</p>

<p>The project financed the generating of 925,585 workdays for coastal family members, including vulnerable, poor, and women-headed households, from work in planting and maintaining shelterbelts, roadside plants, restoring mangroves, and raising saplings in nurseries. Of these workdays, 487,079 workdays were of female workers. </p>

<p>Information source: APFD project completion report. Meeting with the PMU.</p>

<p>This indicator is an new indicator introduced in the September 2020 restructuring.</p>

<p>Target achieved. (1,501% for Total Direct Project Beneficiaries, 1,502% for female)</p>

<p>To achieve this result, the number of direct project beneficiaries of Components 1 (241,377, Female: 120,707), 2 (2,509,153, Female: 1,237,435), 4 (6,029, Female: 3,172) and 5 (34,769,000, Female: 17,036,810) was summed up. Component 3 did not have any direct project beneficiaries. </p>

<p>Under Component 1, the PIU (APEPDCL) reported the number of people with uninterrupted and reliable supply of power through UG cables in Visakhapatnam City covered by the project. APEPDCL assumed 2.9974 as the average person per service connected to UG cable network. Therefore, 241,377 was calculated by multiplying 80,529 (Number of electric consumer accounts covered by the UG cable network) by 2.9974. According to the PIU, the number of female beneficiaries was calculated by the ratio from 2011 Visakhapatnam census data.</p>

<p>Under Component 2, it is the same number as the PDO-level indicator for Component 2 which is the number of peoplewith access to restored and improved rural roads and shelters. As mentioned in the ICR, it is actually the number of people with access to restored and improved rural roads and MDRs. </p>

<p>Under Component 3, most activities were cancelled except for Kaliasagiri Hill Park which was paused and never completed; therefore, the number is reported as zero.</p>

<p>Under Component 4, the number of direct project beneficiaries are people who worked in planting, and maintaining shelterbelts, roadside plants, restoring mangroves, and raising saplings in nurseries. As far as the number of female beneficiaries is concerned, it was the actual number of female workers who participated in the above-mentioned activities.</p>

<p>Under Component 5, APSDMA reported the number of the state population who would get notifications of emergency situations under AP-ALERT as the overarching number of direct project beneficiaries.</p>

<p>Information source: Results provided by the PMU and PIUs, Reviewed and put together by ICR Author.</p>

<p>This indicator is an original IRI which was repositioned as PDO-level indicator in the September 2020 restructuring.</p>

<p>Achieved (111%).</p>

<p>The project financed the planting of 898 hectare of shelterbelts in the existing APFD sites in the four disaster-affected districts, which were damaged by Cyclone Hudhud or subject to degradation due to biotic interference</p>

<p>Information source: Meeting with PMU, APFD project completion report. World Bank Aide Memoires.</p>
